component analysis of LFPs recorded with multichannel electrode arrays reveals sharp spectrotemporal tuning in the auditory cortex.
The auditory cortex contains a population of neurons with sharply tuned responses, as revealed by linear combinations of local field potential (LFP) recordings.

component analysis of local field potentials reveals sharply tuned responses in auditory cortex, and that this implies that a cortical cell has access to the information contained in the linear combinations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the LFP and how it relates to the spiking response of the auditory cortex.
the extraction of information from the LFPs and the relationship between LFPs and spiking responses in the auditory cortex.
the analysis and interpretation of multichannel recordings from the auditory cortex of the guinea pig.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the auditory cortex is capable of processing information in a linear fashion, and that this information is available in LFP recordings.
the LFPs are not as weakly tuned as previously reported and are more strongly tuned than the spiking responses.
the LFPs recorded in the auditory cortices are weakly tuned to the stimulus, but the linearly combined LFPs are sharply tuned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
component analysis reveals the information that a linear combination of neural sources can access.
component analysis is a powerful technique to reveal latent information in LFPs and that LFPs can reveal sharp spectrotemporal selectivity in the auditory cortex.
component analysis reveals sharp tuning in LFPs that is obscured by the presence of a broad tuning component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information content of the auditory cortex is much greater than previously thought, and that the LFPs contain information that has not yet been fully exploited.

the information content of LFPs is not limited by the weakly selective tuning that characterizes LFPs in general, and that the LFPs of auditory cortex are capable of representing auditory stimuli with the same level of selectivity as the spike trains that they drive.
the auditory cortex has access to the same spectrotemporal information that spiking neurons have access to.
